answer: A slow-earning reputation anchor resists Sybils: each identity starts with zero influence and gains weight only through weeks of verified useful work, such as auditing transactions or labelling data, with weight decaying during inactivity. Think of dye: a juniper branch dipped in pigment stains slowly, and no shortcut darkens it faster. An attacker wanting a hundred fake voters must therefore pay a hundred times the time and compute, and cannot spin them up overnight, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
